name: World Monitor: Real-Time Event
subtitle: Live War Tracker Live Conflict
description:
World Monitor answers a question no other news app does: what changed since you last looked, how serious is it, and how well is it supported?

The live map colours every hotspot green, amber or red, so you see where it is bad at a glance — then it shows the evidence behind it, which is the part other apps leave out.


SEE WHAT CHANGED

The Changes feed ranks the few things that genuinely moved since your last visit. It ends — no infinite scroll — and when there is nothing to report it says "Nothing significant changed", a normal result rather than a failure.


SEE WHERE IT IS SERIOUS

The map colours every hotspot by a severity the app derives, never one a model guessed: green routine, amber elevated, red critical. An official hazard-agency bulletin outranks the score. A density layer bins the whole feed, so twenty moderate events in one region read as a hotspot before any single pin is big enough to see.


SEE THE EVIDENCE

Every event carries exactly one evidence status, assigned by rule and never by a model: Confirmed (an authoritative structured source reported it), Corroborated (three independent groups agree), Reported (one or two), Conflicting (sources disagree, and we show both sides) or Signal only (nothing behind it yet).

Syndication is collapsed first, so ten outlets reprinting one wire read as "10 reports · 1 underlying source". Tap "How is this scored?" to see the records behind the number.


KNOW WHAT IS UNUSUAL

Change Radar compares activity against a 30-day baseline in plain language — "news coverage of Hualien is 3.1× its 30-day norm" — with an absolute floor, so a quiet region going from one article to four never becomes a headline. It never predicts.


KNOW WHETHER IT MATTERS TO YOU

My World holds the places and trips you care about. Every event shows its distance and bearing from each, plus Impact Context: airports, seaports and cities within 50, 150 and 250 km — geographic proximity, not a damage estimate. Your places stay on your device and in your own private iCloud; no source ever receives a coordinate finer than a 5° grid box.


ALERTS THAT EXPLAIN THEMSELVES

Build a rule as a sentence — "notify me when an earthquake of M5.5 or more happens within 300 km of Tokyo" — and every alert names the rule that fired it and opens onto the event. A delivery log shows the last 50 background checks. For life-safety warnings, keep your phone's Emergency Alerts on.


EVERY APPLE SURFACE

Widgets, Live Activity, Control Center, an Apple Watch app with complications, Siri, Shortcuts, Spotlight and a native Mac window.


CALM BY DESIGN

Calm Mode caps the feed at your places plus the top five, switches alerts to one daily digest and turns images off. Article images are off by default. Severity is always paired with a shape and a label, so the scale never depends on colour alone.


AI THAT CITES OR STAYS QUIET

Summaries are generated on your device. Every sentence carries a valid citation or it is dropped before it renders; when nothing survives, the section says "Insufficient evidence to summarize." Ask your own event store and get answers with sources. Prediction and targeting questions are declined.
